teaser.text: Compass Group is a company that runs food and support services inside other organisations’ premises. Its business is simple to describe but rich in mechanics: clients hire it to operate daily services, while clients, diners and event-goers supply the money that flows through them.

stock.title: Compass stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Compass stock forecast: weighted scenarios show how earnings, cash conversion, acquisitions and debt shape possible share values.
stock.opening: Compass's weighted value is $31.72 in October 2027, including dividends. It hinges on profitable contract launches, retention, margins and free cash flow that helps reduce absolute debt.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers questions about Compass: its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The weighted value is $31.72 at the first date, implying a 5% total return. It becomes $32.91 at the second date, implying 11%. At the last date, it reaches $34.43, implying 18%. The base case carries 55% probability, while the bear case carries 25%. The bull case carries 20%.
By the last date, the forecast spans $23.84 in the bear case to $46.77 in the bull case, against today’s $30.92. The range is wide because both earnings and the P/E multiple can move together.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Compass, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Bear earnings are $2,175m at the first date and $2,243m at the second, before reaching $2,311m. Bull earnings are $2,345m initially and $2,633m at the second date, then $2,956m. The bear case allows for slower growth, mobilisation delays, acquisition costs and financing pressure. The bull case assumes timely launches, stronger volume, better margins and attractive acquisition returns. Recent evidence supports the range: half-year net income was $1,069m, while June organic growth was 7.1%.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Compass really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations rose from $1,604.27 million in 2021 to $3,366 million in 2025. Free cash flow reached $2,209 million, while “real free cash flow” after stock-based pay reached $2,127 million. Working capital released $186 million in 2024 but absorbed $40 million in 2025, so the later cash performance did not rely on the earlier release.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Compass today?

paragraphs.text: A 26.0x trailing P/E means investors pay a substantial price for the last twelve months of earnings. The 25.1x forward P/E makes a similar demand of expected earnings. The 1.2x enterprise-value-to-revenue ratio looks lower, but revenue includes the food, wages and other costs of serving meals. The 6.6x price-to-book ratio values earning power far above recorded net assets.

blocks.heading: Is Compass's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The latest cash pattern shows the trade-off. Compass paid dividends and bought back shares while also acquiring businesses. Acquisitions absorbed more cash than disposals returned, so the company issued debt and cash fell. Its own net-debt measure differs from a broader measure that includes lease liabilities and other adjustments; neither represents net cash.

earnings.title: Compass earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Compass reports on November 24, 2026; management guides to above 11% underlying operating profit growth and mid-to-high single-digit organic growth.
earnings.opening: Compass’s next results are due on November 24, 2026. The key thing to watch is whether Compass turns contract wins into cash while reducing acquisition-related borrowing.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Compass’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Compass guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Compass’s financial year ends on 30 September. On 11 May 2026, management raised its forecast for FY26 underlying operating profit growth to above 11%, then repeated it on 21 July. Underlying profit excludes specified adjusting items, while constant currency removes the effect of exchange-rate movements. The target concerns operating profit before interest and tax, not the final profit available to shareholders.

Beyond FY26, Compass promises mid-to-high single-digit organic growth, continued margin progression and profit growing faster than revenue. But once an acquisition has been owned for a full year, it no longer supplies the same automatic comparison boost. FY26 results arrive on 24 November 2026; they should not be mistaken for formal FY27 guidance. That makes the analysts’ baseline the next piece of the story.

blocks.heading: Has Compass kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management has also delivered on net new business, meaning revenue from new contracts minus revenue from lost contracts. It was 4.5% in 2025, the fourth consecutive year within the 4%–5% target range. If prior organic revenue were £100, winning £7 and losing £2 would produce 5% net new business. That measure supports organic growth, but it does not guarantee that every new contract will be profitable.

blocks.heading: How have Compass’s revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: For full earnings and cash, the half-year to March 2026 is more useful. Revenue was $24,983 million, against $22,568 million a year earlier. Operating income was $1,605 million, against $1,476 million.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Compass’s next release?

paragraphs.text: The first checkpoint is 24 November 2026, when Compass reports FY26 results. Investors can compare completed-year profit growth with the above-11% promise and examine the starting point for FY27. New guidance will matter more than a repetition of the old target because the latest acquisitions will begin contributing differently to the annual comparison.
